Not expressible in JSON Schema, checked by tsc.

style.description: TS: import("@types/react/index").CSSProperties | ((state: import("@base-ui/react/accordion/index").AccordionPanelState) => import("@types/react/index").CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. Not expressible in JSON Schema, checked by tsc.

x-uikit.intent: The height-animated panel revealed when its AccordionItem is open.
typical_uses: The single body/detail child of an AccordionItem, shown when it is open

invariants.text: Open/close height-animates against Base UI's own `--accordion-panel-height` custom property, a live ResizeObserver measurement written on the panel element - not a themeable token.

anti_patterns.dont: Rely on the panel's content being mounted while its item is closed
anti_patterns.instead: Set `keepMounted` on the Accordion root if closed-panel content must stay in the DOM (e.g. for in-page search); otherwise assume it unmounts

good.title: A panel as an AccordionItem's body
good.code:
<AccordionItem value="item-1">
  <AccordionTrigger>Is it accessible?</AccordionTrigger>
  <AccordionContent>Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.</AccordionContent>
</AccordionItem>

bad.title: A panel with no AccordionItem around it
bad.code: <AccordionContent>Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.</AccordionContent>
bad.why: AccordionContent reads the nearest AccordionItem's open state through Base UI context to decide whether to render; outside one, it has nothing to read.

dont_use_when.rule: Content that must stay visible regardless of any item's open state

assumptions.claim: keepMounted and hiddenUntilFound are usually set on the Accordion root, not per panel
assumptions.reason: Base UI accepts both on the panel as well, and this contract lists them because the panel really does take them; accordion.md documents them on the root, which is where one setting covers every panel of one accordion. Setting them here overrides that root setting for this panel alone.

assumptions.claim: render replaces the panel element with one the caller supplies
assumptions.reason: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the panel's state; neither is expressible in JSON Schema. The panel is the element Base UI writes `--accordion-panel-height` on, so a replaced element still has to be the one the height animation measures.

assumptions.claim: style accepts a function of the panel's state as well as a plain style object
assumptions.reason: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`; a JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form.
